turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I feel caught between you both, as if I am the one who must reconcile these opposing forces. But I am unsure of how to proceed.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am warning you, Sandip, not out of fear, but to protect my people and land. Your actions are unacceptable, and I will not tolerate them.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I am torn between your words, Nikhil, and I see the fire in Sandip's eyes. What is my role in this? Must I choose?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your words burn, Nikhil, but do not mistake my flame for fear. I am here to fight for a cause, not to cower to threats. And Bimala, you need not choose, for we stand together in the fire of revolution.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your revolutionary fire burns hot, but it may consume all in its path. I will not be a bystander to the destruction.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your caution is misplaced. The path of revolution is fraught with danger, but it is a path I am willing to walk. And Bimala, you are my guiding star, my confidant in this fiery struggle.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I am caught between these flames, Sandip, and the calm of Nikhil's words. Can there be a path that honors both my love for you and my respect for my husband?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: My dear Bimala, the fire of revolution is a consuming force, but it is a flame that illuminates the path to freedom. I promise you, there is room in this fire for your love and your conscience. Trust in the passion that binds us.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: My heart is torn, Sandip, but I cannot ignore the warnings from my husband. Can we find a middle ground, a path that does not ignite the fires you speak of?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Bimala, your heart is wise. There is no middle ground in Sandip's fire. It consumes all, leaving nothing but ashes. I urge you to see reason and the dangers that lie ahead.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I see the fire in Sandip's eyes and the caution in Nikhil's words. Both are parts of me, yet I fear the path I choose will hurt one of you. Can we find a way forward that does not end in pain?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: My dearest Bimala, Nikhil's fears are the shadows of a timid heart. The path of revolution is not one of caution but of courage. Trust in the fire that burns within me, for it is the light that will guide us to a brighter future.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, your words may light a fire, but they also spread fear. I come to warn you, not just for myself, but for all of us. Cease your oppressive actions against my people or face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your words are the echoes of a defeated spirit. I see the fear in your eyes, but I also see the pain and suffering of our people. I will not cease my actions until we have justice and equality.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I am caught between two fires, each burning with a different truth. Can we not find a path that honors both courage and compassion?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your caution is a prison, but my fire is the key to our freedom. Bimala, my love, I promise to walk the path of justice with compassion in my heart.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, Nikhil, I feel like a bird caught between two strong winds. Can we not find a way forward that does not leave ashes behind?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, your promises of justice are like the mirage of water in the desert. They may quench the thirst for now, but they offer no lasting solution. I urge you to consider the long-term consequences of your actions.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your fear clouds your vision. My actions may seem oppressive, but they are the hammer that breaks the chains of our oppressors. Bimala, my love, let us build a bridge of understanding and hope.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, Nikhil, I feel torn. Your words, though they clash, hold truths that I cannot ignore. Can we not seek a middle path, one that respects both your visions?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ... No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
